transactions.analysis: Draft baseline Thommy had Jackson, Andrews and Ekeler; Jacobs was acquired from Tony the preceding day. Birch drafted Prescott, Fant, Gibson and Elliott, with Burrow as QB depth. Week 1 Thommy started Prescott (26.42), Fant (9.20), Gibson (9.30); Birch started Jackson (17), Andrews (3.50), Jacobs (16.50). Both changed three starting positions without increasing positional counts.
transactions.verdict: Both rebuilt their starting core; Birch's stronger archived production must be assessed against equal scoring windows and Jacobs' brief prior ownership.

transactions.analysis: Thommy drafted Ekeler, Taylor, Brown and Davis; Tony drafted Hill, Adams, Jacobs, Hunt, Javonte Williams and Robinson. Week 1 Hill started for Thommy (32.60), Javonte benched (4.60), Jacobs already transferred to Birch. Taylor and Brown started for Tony (14.60 and 12.90), Davis benched (24.20). Tony retained Adams; Thommy retained Ekeler and subsequently acquired Gibson.
transactions.verdict: Both pursued quality changes across RB/WR; Jacobs' next-day transfer must not create duplicate direct production. Tony's stronger archive return alone is insufficient to grade Thommy's combined strategy.

transactions.analysis: Week 2 Stew started McCaffrey and Edwards-Helaire (2.60), with Hines and Ty'Son Williams benched. Kuhl started Harris and Henderson while Drake and Barkley were benched. Week 3 Barkley started for Stew (18.40), Drake benched (7.20); Edwards-Helaire (15.90) and Williams (2.20) started for Kuhl, Hines benched (16.40).
transactions.verdict: Stew consolidated backfield assets into a starter; Kuhl converted two reserves into multiple usable RB options. Both have reasonable fit.

transactions.correction: Complete receipt: Stilly acquired AJ Dillon from Mitch for $5 FAAB, no player surrendered. Actual FAAB transfer per provider; spending/disposition unverified.
transactions.analysis: Week 3 Stilly started Jones and Carson; Murray and Gordon on bench. Mitch started Chubb and Davis; Dillon benched (3.60), Jamaal Williams and Ronald Jones also reserves. Week 4 Dillon was on Stilly's bench (10.20). Archive credits 54.40 across five starts, not reconciled.
transactions.verdict: Low-cost RB depth acquisition with later recorded use; Mitch converted a reserve into budget flexibility. Neither side should be graded as a zero-return player swap.

transactions.analysis: Week 3 Evans started Mahomes (22.90), Swift and Harris; Fournette (4.90) and Aiyuk (12.50) benched. Kuhl started Rodgers (18.54), Allen (15), Thielen, Brown and two TEs. Week 4 Rodgers (24.12) and Allen (7.10) started for Evans; Mahomes (31.72) and Aiyuk (2) started for Kuhl, Fournette benched (15.30). Fournette later moved to Stover.
transactions.verdict: Evans consolidated reserve depth into two starters; Kuhl added depth and a starting QB. Direct production and onward Fournette value require separate treatment.

transactions.analysis: Week 4 Koble started Kamara, Mixon and Montgomery; Tony started Taylor, Robinson, Hunt and Patterson, Moss benched. Week 5 Robinson (22.20) and Moss (10.70) started for Koble; Mixon benched (10) for Tony behind Taylor, Mattison and Patterson. Montgomery recorded zero on Koble's bench.
transactions.verdict: Koble added immediate RB flexibility while Tony consolidated an already deep group. Later archive favors Tony in scoring, but initial fit supports Koble.

transactions.analysis: Week 4 Stover started Henry and Sanders at RB, Metcalf, Jefferson, Smith and Chase at WR/FLEX. Kuhl had Fournette benched (15.30) with Edwards-Helaire and Henderson starting. Week 5 Fournette started for Stover (19), Smith started for Kuhl (11.20).
transactions.verdict: Both converted positional depth into starters. Stover's larger archived return supports the realized side, not a claim Kuhl's strategy lacked merit.

transactions.analysis: Week 5 Thommy started Ekeler and Gibson, with Javonte and Mitchell benched; Stew started Collins and Barkley, McCaffrey benched at zero, Cooper starting at WR. Week 6 Cooper started in Thommy FLEX (8), Javonte at RB; Gibson started for Stew (3.40), alongside Booker, with Barkley/McCaffrey benched at zero.
transactions.verdict: Stew addressed observable RB availability pressure and Thommy converted backfield depth into WR help. Both immediate fits reasonable; historical injury evidence not established.

transactions.analysis: Week 5 Stilly started Jones and Murray (4), Carson benched at zero, with Lamb, Diggs, Moore and Johnson in WR/FLEX. Tony had Hunt benched (23.40), Taylor, Mattison and Patterson starting. Week 6 Hunt started for Stilly (9.30), Lamb for Tony (31.60). Archive credits Hunt only 2.80 in one start, creating apparent same-week eligibility discrepancy.
transactions.verdict: Both traded from depth into a starting need. Tony obtained stronger immediate and archived production; Hunt's Week 6 score and ownership window require reconciliation before grading.

transactions.analysis: Week 7 Tony started Seals-Jones at TE (8.10), Kittle benched at zero and Landry benched (6.20); Kuhl started Kelce (10), Pitts benched (19.80). Week 8 Pitts started for Tony (2.30), Kuhl retained Kelce with Kittle (0) and Landry (7.50) benched.
transactions.verdict: Tony converted reserve assets into immediate TE utilization; Kuhl dealt TE surplus for depth. Archive favors Kuhl's later production, but the initial roster context supports both strategies.
